In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the kidney adapts to hyperglycaemic stress and the potential role of the epithelial Na channel (ENaCs) in this process.
understanding how hyperglycaemia leads to secondary hypertension in patients with diabetic nephropathy and the mechanisms involved in the development of renal disease.
the mechanisms by which hyperglycaemia alters the ability of cells to resolve and appropriately respond to sodium resorption in the kidney.

high glucose levels increase Na+ re-absorption in HCD cells by increasing the expression of SGK1, which up-regulates αENaC expression, leading to increased Na+ resorption in HCD-cells.
